title: X5 RetailHero RICH-covariate heterogeneity follow-up (mirrors x5-benchmark/forecaster_x5.py and hillstrom-benchmark/forecaster_powered.py)
objective: Follow-up to the X5-thin generalization MISS (rho +0.163, perm p 0.52, FAIL). Hypothesis: the who-responds-more ranking failed on X5 because the segments used thin DEMOGRAPHIC covariates (age/gender/tenure). Test whether RICH PRE-TREATMENT BEHAVIORAL covariates (purchase-history RFM) recover the ranking on the SAME dataset and SAME RCT ground truth, with richer features.
dataset: X5 RetailHero uplift (scikit-uplift S3 mirror), including purchases.csv.gz
treatment: retailer SMS promotion (treatment_flg=1) vs no-SMS holdout (=0)
pre_treatment_cutoff: 2019-02-19 (purchases STRICTLY before; purchase history spans 2018-11-25..2019-03-18, documented SMS window begins 2019-02-19). This cutoff is an assumption (no explicit treatment-date column); recorded as a limitation.
feature_engineering: Single streaming pass over purchases.csv.gz. Per-client pre-cutoff RFM-style features: recency_days (days from last pre-cutoff txn to cutoff), frequency_txns, active_days, monetary_total, monetary_avg, basket_avg_lines, category_breadth (distinct product_id), redeem_txn_share, earn_total. 380,083 clients have pre-cutoff features.
segment_definition: Independent tertiles (low/mid/high) of Recency x Frequency x Monetary over the eligible population (clients in uplift_train with pre-cutoff features). Tertile cutpoints computed from FEATURES ONLY (never from uplift). 3x3x3 = up to 27 cells; cells with < 200 per arm dropped. Cutpoints: recency [2.0,7.0] days, frequency [7.0,17.0] txns, monetary [2929.0,6764.0].

method.probe: per-segment blinded expert-forecaster, mirroring forecaster_x5.py / forecaster_powered.py
method.framing: expert in retail SMS-promotion causal effects; predicts treatment-vs-holdout uplift for each audience described from PRE-TREATMENT behavioral features ONLY (recency/frequency/monetary tiers + basket size, category breadth, redeem share). Real uplift NEVER shown.
method.output: numeric predicted responsiveness (predicted uplift in percentage points) per segment
method.blinding: audience descriptions built from behavioral features only; no uplift, no target rates, no ranking leaked
method.seeds: 4000 + segment_index (distinct from thin run's 3000+ to avoid any cache collision)

scoring.primary: Spearman rank-rho between predicted scores and REAL per-segment uplift (repo spearman_rho, same as Hillstrom/thin)
scoring.significance: label-permutation p-value on |rho|, 5000 shuffles, seed=42 (mirrors perm_p)

pre_registered_bar.description: SAME bar as Hillstrom and the X5-thin run

registered_prediction: We EXPECT rich behavioral covariates to RECOVER the ranking better than the thin demographic run, and we register a directional bet that the bar is cleared (rho > 0.30, p < 0.05) — moderate confidence. Rationale: the real per-segment uplift carries a clear engagement/ceiling structure (low-monetary, low-frequency customers have the most room to be moved by an SMS and show the largest uplift; high-spend/high-frequency customers are near their ceiling and show near-zero or negative uplift). An expert retail-marketing forecaster should plausibly anticipate this 'reach the under-engaged' pattern from RFM tiers, which the purely demographic descriptions could not express. Counter-risk we acknowledge: a single Sonnet forecaster may instead apply a naive 'engaged customers respond more' prior (the OPPOSITE of the truth here), which would drive rho negative; and 26 segments with a 3-way interaction is a harder rank task than Hillstrom's. So recovery is plausible but not assured.
stopping_rule: Run all 26 segments once at temperature 0.0; no peeking, no segment re-selection after seeing predictions, no re-tuning of descriptions after seeing rho. Result is whatever this single pre-registered run produces.
